questions.title: Assign the Cookies
questions.description:
A bakery hands cookies to children: child i is content only with a cookie of size at least greed[i], and each cookie feeds at most one child. The greedy rule: sort both lists, then give each least-greedy child the smallest cookie that satisfies them. Maximize the content children. No imports — pure Python only (sort with sorted).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def content_children(greed, sizes):

greed is the list of children's greed factors and sizes the cookie sizes. Sort both with sorted, sweep with two pointers, and return how many children can be made content.

Input Format:
Line 1: the greed factors, space-separated.
Line 2: the cookie sizes, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the number of content children.

Constraints:

questions.title: Load the Truck
questions.description:
A delivery truck has limited box slots; each box type offers a number of boxes and the units each box carries. Load greedily by units per box (highest first), taking as many whole boxes as the slots allow, and report the total units loaded.

The program scaffolding (input reading and pair building) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def max_units(box_types, truck_size):

box_types is a list of (count, units_per_box) pairs. Sort the types by units_per_box descending, take whole boxes from the best types while slots remain, and return the total units.

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the number of box types.
Next n lines: count units_per_box.
Last line: the truck size (box slots).

Output Format:
One line with the maximum total units.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= count[i], units_per_box[i] <= 1000
0 <= truck_size <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
def read_pairs(n):
    pairs = []
    for _ in range(n):
        a, b = map(int, input().split())
        pairs.append((a, b))
    return pairs


def max_units(box_types, truck_size):
    order = sorted(box_types, key=lambda b: b[1], reverse=True)
    total = 0
    space = truck_size
    for cnt, units in order:
        take = cnt if cnt < space else space
        total += take * units
        space -= take
        if space == 0:
            break
    return total


def main():
    n = int(input())
    box_types = read_pairs(n)
    truck_size = int(input())
    print(max_units(box_types, truck_size))


main()

questions.title: Canonical Coin Counter
questions.description:
A vending machine stocks the canonical denominations 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000 (given to you sorted largest-first). For canonical systems the greedy choice — repeat the largest coin that fits — is provably optimal. Count the coins dispensed for an amount. No imports — pure Python only.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_coins(amount, coins):

amount is the value to pay and coins the denomination list sorted descending. Sweep the list taking floor divisions and remainders, and return the total number of coins.

Input Format:
One line: the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the number of coins.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 100000
coins is exactly the canonical set, sorted descending
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= amount <= 100000; coins is the canonical set sorted descending
questions.sourcecode:
CANONICAL_COINS = [1000, 500, 100, 50, 20, 10, 5, 2, 1]


def min_coins(amount, coins):
    count = 0
    for c in coins:
        count += amount // c
        amount %= c
    return count


def main():
    amount = int(input())
    print(min_coins(amount, CANONICAL_COINS))


main()

questions.title: Rescue Boats
questions.description:
A flood rescue team has boats that carry at most limit kilograms and at most TWO people per trip. The greedy pairing rule: sort the weights, then try to pair the heaviest survivor with the lightest one — sail whoever fits. Count the minimum number of trips. No imports — pure Python only (sort with sorted).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_boats(people, limit):

people is the list of survivor weights and limit the boat capacity (every weight fits alone). Sort with sorted, then sweep with two indices from both ends, and return the minimum number of boats.

Input Format:
Line 1: the weights, space-separated.
Line 2: the boat limit.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of boats.

Constraints:
1 <= len(people) <= 1000
1 <= people[i] <= limit <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def min_boats(people, limit):
    people = sorted(people)
    i = 0
    j = len(people) - 1
    boats = 0
    while i <= j:
        if people[i] + people[j] <= limit:
            i += 1
        j -= 1
        boats += 1
    return boats


def main():
    people = list(map(int, input().split()))
    limit = int(input())
    print(min_boats(people, limit))


main()

questions.title: Jobs Before Deadlines
questions.description:
A workshop runs jobs one at a time starting at time 0; job i takes durations[i] minutes and must FINISH by deadlines[i]. The greedy rule: sort by deadline and schedule each job as early as possible, skipping any job that would overrun its deadline. Maximize the number of completed jobs. No imports — pure Python only (sort with sorted).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def max_jobs(durations, deadlines):

durations and deadlines pair up by index. Sort the (duration, deadline) pairs by deadline, sweep keeping the current time, and return how many jobs can be completed.

Input Format:
Line 1: the durations, space-separated.
Line 2: the deadlines, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of jobs completed.

Constraints:
1 <= len(durations) <= 1000
1 <= durations[i], deadlines[i] <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
def max_jobs(durations, deadlines):
    pairs = sorted(zip(durations, deadlines), key=lambda p: p[1])
    now = 0
    count = 0
    for d, dl in pairs:
        if now + d <= dl:
            now += d
            count += 1
    return count


def main():
    durations = list(map(int, input().split()))
    deadlines = list(map(int, input().split()))
    print(max_jobs(durations, deadlines))


main()

questions.title: Join the Ropes
questions.description:
A climbing gym fuses n rope strands into one. Every fusion joins two strands and costs the SUM of their lengths (the fused strand keeps the combined length). The greedy choice: always fuse the two SHORT strands available. Compute the minimum total fusion cost. No imports or heapq — keep a sorted working list and reinsert with a small scan. No imports — pure Python only.

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_rope_cost(ropes):

ropes is the list of strand lengths. While more than one strand remains, remove the two shortest, add their sum to the total cost, and insert the fused strand back keeping the list sorted. Return the total cost.

Input Format:
One line: the rope lengths, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total cost.

Constraints:
1 <= len(ropes) <= 100
1 <= ropes[i] <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def min_rope_cost(ropes):
    parts = sorted(ropes)
    total = 0
    while len(parts) > 1:
        a = parts.pop(0)
        b = parts.pop(0)
        fused = a + b
        total += fused
        i = 0
        while i < len(parts) and parts[i] < fused:
            i += 1
        parts.insert(i, fused)
    return total


def main():
    ropes = list(map(int, input().split()))
    print(min_rope_cost(ropes))


main()

questions.title: Minimum Platforms
questions.description:
A rail terminus needs enough platforms so no train waits: train i arrives at arrivals[i] and leaves at departures[i]. A train arriving exactly when another departs CANNOT reuse that platform — equal times count as overlapping. Sort both time lists independently and sweep with two pointers, tracking how many trains sit in the station simultaneously. Report the platform minimum. No imports — pure Python only (sort with sorted).

The scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def min_platforms(arrivals, departures):

arrivals and departures list the same trains (pairing lost on sort is fine — the sweep only counts). Sort both with sorted, walk with two indices, and return the maximum simultaneous-train count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the train count.
Line 2: the arrival times, space-separated.
Line 3: the departure times, space-separated.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of platforms.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= arrival[i] <= departure[i] <= 2359
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000; 0 <= arrival[i] <= departure[i] <= 2359; equal arrival/departure counts as overlapping
questions.sourcecode:
def min_platforms(arrivals, departures):
    arrivals = sorted(arrivals)
    departures = sorted(departures)
    best = 1
    i = 0
    n = len(arrivals)
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and arrivals[j] == arrivals[i]:
            j += 1
        if j - i > best:
            best = j - i
        i = j
    return best


def main():
    n = int(input())
    arrivals = list(map(int, input().split()))
    departures = list(map(int, input().split()))
    print(min_platforms(arrivals, departures))


main()
